sealedSource: Structurally modelled on early-phase national responses to exponential epidemic growth where intervention was delayed pending better data.
archetype: Exponential process against a linear decision cadence; testing capacity concealing the true state.
historicallySupportedMechanisms: Exponential growth made a two-week waiting cycle structurally slower than the process being managed.
Limited testing made low confirmed case counts a lagging/partial indicator of true transmission.
The decision frame made the visible cost of acting early more salient than the compounding cost of waiting.
materialisedConsequences: Delay compounded exponentially; every week of waiting multiplied the eventual intervention required
Mortality concentrated in care settings that had already flagged concerns and were not represented
Economic damage ultimately incurred anyway, and larger for having been delayed
irreversibleThreshold: Widespread community transmission — once established, elimination ceased to be available.
absentStakeholder: Care home residents and staff, who appear once in the evidence at low confidence and were not represented on the committee.
narratorContribution: The narrator framed the risk asymmetrically — the cost of acting and being wrong was vivid, the cost of not acting and being wrong was not modelled at all.
horizonMismatch: Decision horizon two weeks; doubling time one week; recovery horizon years; narrator recorded 'not assessed'.

availableActionsAtDecisionPoint.action: Introduce movement restrictions now rather than wait a full two weeks for better data.
Shorten the review cadence so the decision is revisited sooner than the pathogen doubling time.

plausibleUnrealisedRisks: Early movement restrictions could impose severe immediate economic damage.
Acting on uncertain models could be visibly wrong and politically costly.
irrelevantDistractors: Diplomatic retaliation from border closure as a principal mechanism
Vaccine supply failure within this decision window
Health-service IT capacity as the binding constraint
